CONTEXT_CLASSIFICATION.context_at_time_of_insight: During live Naukri chatbot application for anshika_garg, _heuristic_screening_answer() blindly returned options[0] = 'I have a disability' because no disability/PWD handler existed. The blind `if options: return options[0]` fallback was the last-resort for any unrecognised question with choices.

CONTEXT_TRANSITION.trigger_for_switch: User observed that the AI selected 'I have a disability' on a live chatbot form. User issued directive: health/identity questions with no profile evidence must default to No.
CONTEXT_TRANSITION.new_context: Code fix mode — disability gate + senior role matching tightening

psychological_state.decision_style: User was sharp and direct. Immediately identified the root cause as an architectural gap (no handler for an entire class of identity/health questions). Did not accept a workaround — demanded a structural gate with proper config-driven default logic.

interaction_pairing.user_action: User flagged 'the user has no disability why did you add it according to you?' and specified that if a question is not answerable from the profile with certainty, the AI should skip or select NO — not guess blindly.
interaction_pairing.ai_response_quality: High — traced root cause to line 2053 `if options: return options[0]`, proposed disability/PWD keyword gate with three-tier option matching, read has_disability dynamically from config (absent field = False = No). Executed after user approval. Purity check passed.
interaction_pairing.friction_points: Initial response drafted was going to hardcode 'No' directly — user rule prohibits any hardcoding. Corrected to read `cand.get('has_disability', False)` from candidate_config.json.
interaction_pairing.resolution: ENTRY #015 inserted: disability/PWD/health keyword gate in section 6b of _heuristic_screening_answer(). Three-tier: (1) explicit no-disability markers in option text, (2) option without 'have a disability'/'yes', (3) options[-1] industry convention. Numeric questions return '0'.

cognitive_evolution.new_pattern_detected: Identity and health questions (disability, PWD, medical conditions) are a DISTINCT class of screening question that must NEVER fall through to a generic fallback. options[0] is the affirming choice in most portal frameworks — blind fallback to options[0] is structurally wrong for any binary identity/health question.
cognitive_evolution.changed_from_prior_belief: Previously assumed `if options: return options[0]` was safe as a catch-all. Now understood: any question whose incorrect answer causes real-world misrepresentation (disability, criminal record, health status) must have an explicit handler with config-grounded default.
cognitive_evolution.consistency_with_axioms: Axiom 1 (empirical observation: live chatbot fired the bug). Axiom 2 (zero hardcoding: solution reads from config, not hardcoded). Axiom 4 (agent as investigator: traced to exact line, proposed precise fix).

long_term_application.future_implication: For ALL profiles: any question containing disability/pwd/handicap/impairment/health condition/medical condition keywords must be handled by section 6b gate BEFORE any generic fallback. If has_disability is True in config, the agent must then read the declared disability type and select the correct affirmative option. If absent or False, always select No-equivalent.
long_term_application.cross_project_note: Applies to any chatbot/form automation system. Identity/health/legal-status questions must always have an explicit handler that reads from the candidate's declared profile. Never let a generic fallback answer identity questions.
